title: Linen summer wrap
subtitle: A light dc mesh rectangle in sport-weight linen blend, worked with a ch-1 skip-1 pattern
excerpt: This wrap measures 190 cm wide by 55 cm deep and is worked in a simple dc mesh: double crochet separated by single chain spaces with one stitch skipped between each double crochet. The result is a breathable, semi-open fabric in sport-weight linen blend on a 3.5 mm hook. Suitable for crocheters who know double crochet.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. DC mesh construction is a widely established technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A fine rectangular crochet wrap in natural linen-tone sport weight yarn draped loosely over one shoulder and across the body, photographed outdoors in bright natural light, showing the open mesh texture.

crochet.gaugeText: 20 dc-mesh sts x 20 rows = 10 x 10 cm in sport-weight linen blend with a 3.5 mm hook, where each "mesh st" counts as 1 dc plus the following ch-1 space.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approximately 190 cm wide x 55 cm deep, after blocking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A regular fabric of double crochet stitches separated by single chain spaces, with one stitch skipped between each dc. The chain spaces create a grid-like open texture.

For dc mesh, a ch-3 at the start of each row stands in for the first dc plus the following ch-1 space. The pattern then begins by skipping the first dc of the previous row and working into the first ch-1 space.

content.text: throughout: one double crochet (UK), one chain, one skipped stitch, repeated across the row. The stitch produces a lightweight grid fabric that suits sport-weight linen-blend yarns, which block flat and hold their shape without stretching. The wrap lies flat against the body or drapes from the shoulders.

is ch 3 at the start of each row: this stands in for the first dc plus ch-1 space. On every row, the first real dc is worked into the first ch-1 space of the previous row (not into the first skipped stitch or the dc above it). The last dc of each row is worked into the 2nd ch of the turning chain from the row below.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 300 g sport-weight linen-blend yarn. A 3.5 mm crochet hook (US E/4). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure. Optional: blocking mat and pins for a crisper finish.

content.text: 20 mesh sts x 20 rows = 10 x 10 cm in sport-weight linen blend with a 3.5 mm hook. A mesh stitch is one dc plus the following ch-1 space. Work a swatch of at least 30 mesh sts and 24 rows. Count the central 20 sts and 20 rows to check. Linen opens up noticeably with wet blocking, so measure the swatch after blocking if you intend to block the finished wrap.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).

The wrap is worked flat in rows from one short end to the other. The foundation chain sets the long edge (190 cm). Each row adds one layer of mesh across the 55 cm width. The ch-3 turning chain at the start of every row counts as the first dc plus ch-1 space.
Ch 381. This is an odd number plus 2 chains for the turning chain. The 380 working chains become 190 mesh repeats (190 dc and 190 ch-1 spaces), giving 190 cm at the stated gauge.
Ch 3 (counts as dc + ch 1). Skip 2 ch. *1 dc in next ch. Ch 1. Skip 1 ch*; repeat from * to * across. 1 dc in last ch. Turn. (190 dc + 189 ch-1 spaces = 379 sts total)
Ch 3 (counts as dc + ch 1). Skip the first dc. *1 dc in next ch-1 space. Ch 1*; repeat from * to * across. 1 dc in 2nd ch of turning ch. Turn. (190 dc)
Repeat Row 2 on every row. After Row 110 the piece measures approximately 55 cm deep. Fasten off.

attrs.title: Counting check
attrs.body: Each row should contain 190 dc. Count after the first few rows to confirm the mesh is consistent. The most common error is working into the dc of the previous row instead of into the ch-1 space between dc stitches, which collapses the mesh.

content.text: Fasten off and weave in all ends. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, pressing out excess moisture, and pinning the wrap to 190 x 55 cm on a blocking mat. Linen relaxes well with blocking and the mesh spaces open to full width. Leave until completely dry.
Handwash in cool water. Linen becomes softer with each wash. Lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry.

Work the same mesh in a DK cotton on a 4 mm hook for a heavier, warmer version. Replace the ch-1 spaces with ch-2 spaces and skip 2 stitches for a larger open mesh with a lacier look. A simple dc border around all four edges of the finished rectangle gives a firm, non-rolling selvedge.
